newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X CEO has concerns about Busang deal.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X CEO has concerns about Busang deal.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp still have "concerns" about working together to develop the huge Busang gold deposit in Indonesia, Bre-X chief executive officer David Walsh said on Monday.
"We've made a submission ... which says we can work together if the government can satisfy requests by both parties on a couple of items," Walsh said in a phone interview from New York.
"Within the document, there were certain concerns that we've asked the government to give us guidance on," he said. "They are concerns from both parties."

Bre-X and Barrick said in separate statements on Monday that they had presented a joint statement to the Indonesian government about developing Busang, which contains at least 57 million ounces of gold.
The companies said the government would respond to their proposed arrangement "in due course."
"I think it's a workable arrangement," said Walsh. "We're all pleased that we're moving forward."
He said he could not comment on the structure or terms of the proposed deal. But he said price was not one of the issues needing "guidance" from the Indonesian government.
Walsh would not say if shareholders would have a chance to vote on any deal formed with Barrick.
While Walsh said the joint proposal would help make Indonesia, its people and Bre-X shareholders happy, he would not go so far as to call the proposal a "memorandum of understanding."
"We have to wait to see what the government does," he said.

Indonesia asked the two companies in November to form a joint venture to develop the deposit discovered by Bre-X. The government suggested that Barrick get 75 percent, Bre-X keep 25 percent and the two companies arrange for the Indonesian government to receive a 10 percent cut.
Barrick spokesman Vince Borg said earlier Monday that the joint submission "is in accord with the government parameters."
